Lumen is the trusted network for the AI‑powered world, connecting people, data, and applications through our expansive fiber network and connected ecosystem. We enable secure, high‑performance connectivity across cloud, edge, and AI workloads for enterprises, governments, and communities.

At Lumen, you’ll work on infrastructure customers rely on today and build for what’s next, where performance, security, and resilience matter.

This is a high accountability environment where bold ideas drive real innovation for our customers, partners, and industry. The work is challenging, expectations are clear, and trust is built into how we operate. If you’re ready to take ownership, deliver meaningful impact, and help shape the future of AI‑ready connectivity, join us today.

Location

This is a remote position open to candidates based anywhere in the U.S.

The Role

At Lumen, the Lead Information Security Engineer owns the development, maintenance, and defensibility of the security authorization package for assigned systems, ensuring compliance with federal requirements and readiness for assessment. In this role, you apply and refine your RMF expertise through end-to-end execution, working directly with customers and stakeholders to validate controls, surface risk, and drive remediation. Your impact is measured through the successful sustainment of Authorization to Operate (ATO) outcomes, the strength of the system’s security posture, and the ability to support secure, compliant delivery of mission-critical services.

The Lead ISSO may operate independently for smaller or less complex environments or in alignment with a Senior Lead (ISSM) for larger programs.

The successful candidate will demonstrate the ability to:

  • Serve as the primary ISSO for assigned systems, accountable for end-to-end RMF execution and ATO outcomes
  • Execute the full RMF lifecycle, including categorization, control implementation, assessment readiness, authorization support, and continuous monitoring
  • Develop, maintain, and ensure accuracy of authorization artifacts (e.g., SSP, POA&M, control evidence)
  • Ensure systems remain ATO-compliant, audit-ready, and aligned with federal requirements (e.g., FedRAMP, FISMA, DoD)
  • Track, prioritize, and drive remediation of vulnerabilities, audit findings, and control deficiencies
  • Provide system-level risk assessments and actionable recommendations, including impact and remediation considerations
  • Monitor vulnerability, audit, and continuous monitoring data to maintain awareness of system risk posture
  • Coordinate with engineering, operations, and program teams to ensure security controls are implemented effectively and sustainably
  • Support security assessments, audits, and inspections as the ISSO representative, including direct interaction with assessors and customer stakeholders
  • Evaluate products, services, and proposed architectures for compliance, risk, and implementation feasibility within customer authorization environments
  • Support customer integration of managed services by defining control responsibilities, inheritance boundaries, and implementation expectations
  • Provide input grounded in RMF execution and ATO processes to support solution design, capture efforts, and delivery alignment

The Main Responsibilities

  • Strong working knowledge of NIST RMF (SP 800-37) and NIST SP 800-53 control framework
  • Demonstrated experience executing RMF activities and supporting or leading ATO outcomes for federal or DoD systems
  • Experience with FedRAMP and/or FISMA authorization processes, including artifact development and assessment readiness
  • Ability to independently execute RMF activities and manage system-level security posture with minimal oversight
  • Strong understanding of control implementation, inheritance, and shared responsibility models within complex or hybrid environments
  • Ability to assess and communicate security risk in complex architectures, translating regulatory requirements into actionable guidance
  • Experience evaluating security, compliance, and delivery feasibility of products, services, and architectures
  • Working knowledge of cryptographic principles and emerging standards, including post-quantum cryptography (PQC), and ability to assess vendor solutions for compliance, risk, and implementation considerations
  • Strong collaboration skills across engineering, operations, program management, and security teams
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills for both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Demonstrates Lumen leadership behaviors (teamwork, trust, transparency, clarity, courage, customer focus, growth mindset, respect)

What We Look For in a Candidate

  • Bachelor’s degree in information assurance, cybersecurity, or a related field, or equivalent experience
  • Minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in information assurance, with demonstrated responsibility for RMF execution and ATO support
  • Proven experience developing and maintaining authorization artifacts (e.g., SSP, POA&M) and supporting security assessments
  • Experience operating in customer-facing or services-based environments supporting federal or regulated clients is strongly preferred
  • Relevant certifications in governance, risk, and compliance (e.g., CGRC, CISA) are strongly preferred or equivalent demonstrated RMF experience
  • Broad security certifications (e.g., CISSP, CCSP) are preferred and may supplement GRC experience
  • Proficiency with technologies, tools, and processes supporting GRC, vulnerability management, and continuous monitoring

Security Requirements

  • US citizenship required.
  • The capability to meet the suitability requirements for a GSA public trust position is required.

Lumen is the trusted network for the AI‑powered world, connecting people, data, and applications through our expansive fiber network and connected ecosystem. We enable secure, high‑performance connectivity across cloud, edge, and AI workloads for enterprises, governments, and communities.

This is a high accountability environment where bold ideas drive real innovation for our customers, partners, and industry. The work is challenging, expectations are clear, and trust is built into how we operate. If you’re ready to take ownership, deliver meaningful impact, and help shape the future of AI‑ready connectivity, join us today.

The Role

In a consumption-based business, revenue isn't won at contract signature—it's earned every day. That makes Finance a critical strategic partner, sitting at the center of the decisions that drive growth, profitability, and customer success. In this role, you'll work directly with executive leaders to influence pricing, structure complex deals, guide capital allocation, and shape the metrics that define business performance. If you're looking for a role where your insights directly impact company strategy—not just reporting results after the fact—this is it.

The Senior Director of Finance – Consumption Business Partner is a senior finance leadership role within Lumen, serving as the primary finance partner to the Chief Revenue Officer (CRO) for consumption-based revenue and reporting into Business Finance. This is one of the most analytically demanding and commercially influential finance roles in the business: revenue is inherently variable, forecasting is a competitive advantage, and — unlike seat-based SaaS — there is no clean ARR number to anchor the plan. Revenue is a function of what customers actually use.

This position partners closely with the CRO leadership team, Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Customer Success, Product Finance, COGS finance and the enterprise consumption-modeling (Data Finance) team to ensure commercial decisions are grounded in sound financial analysis. The role focuses on forecast narrative, pipeline-to-consumption conversion, customer and segment risk & opportunity, deal economics, and go-to-market efficiency — translating enterprise model outputs and usage economics into clear commercial implications, trade-offs, and recommendations.

The overriding objective is to enable better CRO decisions and forecast explainability — on deals, pricing guardrails, and go-to-market investment — by turning complex consumption dynamics into a clear financial narrative and actionable recommendations.

Work Location

This is a work from home position within the U.S.

The Main Responsibilities

Main Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary finance partner to the CRO and CRO leadership team for consumption-based revenue, and act as the finance voice in major commercial decisions.
  • Translate enterprise consumption forecasts and usage economics into commercial insights, forecast narratives, and action plans across segments, customers, pipeline, and go-to-market motions.
  • Provide finance support on pricing guardrails and deal structures without owning enterprise models, product assumptions, or cost foundations.

Forecast Narrative, Planning & Business Reviews

  • Translate enterprise consumption forecasts into CRO forecast narratives and rolling outlooks spanning committed ARR, consumption run rates, draw-down schedules, and overage projections.
  • Lead monthly business reviews (MBRs) with CRO leadership, providing insight into consumption trends, forecast risks, and plan variances.
  • Apply committed-to-consumed revenue bridges to quantify gaps between contractual commitments and expected revenue consumption, and explain key drivers.
  • Analyze the pipeline-to-commitment-to-consumption conversion path, identifying where bookings are strong but consumption is lagging.
  • Partner with Revenue Operations to ensure CRM, usage, and financial data align and support a consistent commercial narrative.

Performance, Customer & Segment Analytics

  • Own customer- and segment-level revenue risk and opportunity analysis, translating usage-health signals into quantified financial impacts.
  • Maintain portfolio health KPIs, including consumption rates, draw-down velocity, overage revenue, usage NRR, consumption churn, and usage-based LTV.
  • Identify early warning signs of consumption risk and quantify revenue impact before churn events occur.
  • Deliver cohort-level analysis on consumption growth, usage contraction, and overage-driven expansion while differentiating structural and seasonal trends.
  • Partner with Customer Success on usage-health scoring and post-sale consumption strategies.

Deal Economics, Pricing & GTM Efficiency

  • Serve as the CRO's finance partner on consumption-based deal structures, including committed-spend floors, overage rates, discount tiers, and draw-down terms.
  • Model the economics of large deals to assess whether commitments align with expected usage.
  • Support pricing-model evaluations, including pure consumption, hybrid, and tiered usage models, along with ASC 606 revenue-recognition considerations.
  • Maintain discount guardrails and approval thresholds in partnership with Sales Operations and Legal.
  • Provide financial insights on GTM efficiency, including CAC payback, usage-driven expansion, seller productivity, and demand-generation ROI.

Cross-Functional Partnership & Leadership

  • Collaborate with Revenue Finance, Product Finance, Data Finance, and COGS teams to maintain a single, integrated financial perspective.
  • Partner with the CRO and HR to design compensation plans and SPIFs that align seller behavior with consumed revenue.
  • Contribute revenue organization insights to executive, senior leadership, and Board materials through enterprise FP&A processes.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor, influencing commercial decisions through data-driven analysis and storytelling.
  • Drive continuous improvement of consumption-finance processes, tools, and analytical capabilities.

What We Look For in a Candidate

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.
  • 12+ years of progressive experience in financial planning and analysis, business finance, or commercial finance, including senior-level business partnering.
  • Direct experience with consumption-, usage-based, or hybrid pricing models, and building or leveraging usage-based revenue forecast models.
  • Prior experience supporting a revenue, sales, or commercial organization (e.g., CRO), including exposure to deal-desk or commercial-finance structures.
  • Strong analytical and financial modeling skills, including dynamic, scenario-based forecasting.
  • Excellent communication and executive presence, with the confidence to challenge senior stakeholders with data-driven insights and translate financial concepts for non-finance audiences.
  • Strong data fluency and experience working with large usage datasets.
  • Solid understanding of ASC 606 revenue recognition, including variable consideration, usage-based contracts, and pre-purchase arrangements.
  • Proficiency with financial systems and tools such as Excel, Power BI, and CRM platforms (e.g., Salesforce).
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, matrixed environment with strong adaptability, collaboration, and results orientation.

Preferred

  • Experience in cloud infrastructure, data platforms, API-first, or other consumption-based businesses.
  • SQL skills and familiarity with usage-data platforms and data warehouses, including Snowflake, Databricks, and BigQuery.
  • Experience with complex contract structures, including committed spend, overages, and draw-down mechanics.
  • Familiarity with consumption-based sales compensation and quota-attainment models.

German-Speaking Customer Service Agent (Live Chat)

Full-Time| Remote | Flexible, On-Demand Hours

About The Global Talent Co.

We connect exceptional global talent with innovative technology and lifestyle companies worldwide. Our mission: everyone deserves equal access to opportunity, regardless of where they were born. Join our community of 25,000+ professionals building meaningful careers with leading international companies.

About the Company You'll Be Working With

You'll be joining a high-energy, fast-growing European consumer brand in the drinks space — with a strong digital presence, a passionate customer base, and a culture that genuinely cares about experience. This is a lean, dynamic team where your work has a direct and visible impact.

The Opportunity

We're building a bench of German-Speaking Customer Service Agents to support the brand's DACH customers during peak periods. This isn't a standard fixed-hours role — it's a flexible, on-demand arrangement built around the brand's busiest moments.

Here's how it works: agents are guaranteed a baseline of 40–60 hours per month, scheduled as needed around campaign activity. The brand runs a campaign every month, so there's regular, predictable work — plus bigger seasonal peaks like Black Week and the pre-Christmas period, where demand (and hours) increase further. Agents who are open to picking up additional hours during these spikes will have the opportunity to do so.

This is a live chat-only role. You won't be on the phone — but you will be the face of the brand in writing, so strong written German is just as important as your customer service instincts. You'll be handling customer enquiries, resolving complaints, and making sure every interaction reflects the brand's standards.

Because the work is concentrated around campaign bursts (typically 1–2 weeks at a time), we're looking for agents who are genuinely available and responsive during these windows, even if the exact days and hours have some flexibility.

If you take pride in clear communication, stay calm when things get busy, and know your way around an ecommerce environment — we'd love to hear from you.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Handling customer enquiries and complaints via live chat — professionally, promptly, and in German

  • Flexing your availability up during campaign peaks, including monthly campaigns and seasonal peaks like Black Week and pre-Christmas

  • Resolving issues with empathy and efficiency, ensuring customers feel heard and helped

  • Representing the brand's voice accurately across every interaction

  • Identifying recurring issues or patterns and flagging them to the wider team

  • Keeping records accurate and up to date

  • Collaborating with internal teams where needed to resolve customer issues end-to-end

What We're Looking For

  • Native or near-native German speaker — this is a firm requirement; all customer communication is in German

  • Excellent written German — clear, warm, and professional; this will be assessed during the interview process

  • Prior experience in an ecommerce environment — you understand how online retail works and what customers expect

  • Some background in customer-facing communication, whether via chat, email, or phone

  • Calm under pressure and comfortable handling complaints or difficult interactions with professionalism

  • Genuinely available for on-demand scheduling — comfortable with a flexible, campaign-driven workload rather than fixed weekly hours

  • Able to commit to a baseline of 40–60 hours per month, with openness to additional hours during peak periods

  • Reliable and self-motivated — you manage your own schedule and follow through on your commitments

  • Comfortable working remotely and independently within a structured team environment

What's On Offer

  • Competitive hourly rate (discussed during the interview process)

  • Fully remote position — work from anywhere

  • Guaranteed baseline of 40–60 hours per month, with the opportunity to pick up more during peak periods

  • Flexible scheduling within each campaign window

  • Paid annual leave

  • Exposure to a fast-moving, high-growth consumer brand

  • Access to The Global Talent Co.'s wider professional community of 25,000+ global professionals

At The Global Talent Co., we believe great talent exists everywhere. We're proud to connect professionals across the globe with companies that value what they bring.

raw.description:
At Gardens Interactive, we're building games centered on connection, collective adventure, and emergent stories. We're creating magical, shared experiences that bring players together, and we know those experiences come from teams that are curious, resilient, ambitious, and deeply committed to one another.

We're a fully remote studio that embraces collaboration, thoughtful iteration, and the courage to explore new ideas. If you enjoy solving difficult problems with kind, talented teammates and want to help build worlds where friendships flourish, we'd love to meet you.

As our Lead Game Engineer, you will...

Team Leadership

  • Manage, mentor, and grow a team of game engineers: set goals, run 1:1s, give feedback, and support career development.

  • Plan, recruit, and interview technical roles within the Gameplay Engineering team.

  • Own team processes: planning, code review standards, on-call/bug triage, and how work gets scoped and estimated.

  • Create a healthy, high-trust engineering culture at a small-studio scale.

Hands-on Development

  • Review pull requests and unblock engineers on hard technical problems.

  • Debug and resolve complex cross-system issues, especially around multiplayer sync, performance, and stability.

  • Prototype or build out gameplay systems directly when the team needs an extra pair of hands.

Cross-functional Collaboration

  • Partner closely with game design, art, and production to scope features and keep engineering aligned with the creative vision.

  • Partner with the Technical Director to create a realistic technical roadmap.

  • Communicate engineering status, risks, and trade-offs clearly to studio leadership.

What You'll Bring

  • 6+ years of professional game development experience, with shipped title(s) built in Unreal Engine.

  • 2+ years of experience directly managing or leading engineers (formal management, tech lead, or team lead experience).

  • Strong C++ skills and deep familiarity with Blueprint workflows.

  • Hands-on experience with online multiplayer systems, including replication, client-server architecture, netcode, and the performance/debugging challenges that come with them.

  • Solid grasp of software architecture and design patterns, and the judgment to know when to apply them versus keep things simple.

  • Experience working cross-functionally with design, art, and production in a real production environment.

  • Comfortable operating with high ownership in a lean team where you wear multiple hats.

  • Strong communication skills: able to explain technical trade-offs to non-engineers and rally a small team around a plan.

Nice to Have

  • Experience shipping a live-service or online multiplayer game post-launch (patching, live ops, backend services).

  • Experience at an independent or mid-size studio.

  • Experience with performance profiling and optimization.

The Team

  • Reports to the Technical Director.

  • Leads the Gameplay Engineering team.

  • Partners closely with the Backend Lead, Technical Director, Production, Design, Art, QA, and the broader engineering organization.

How We Work

We believe great games are built by people who care deeply about both the work and one another. Our values guide how we collaborate, solve problems, make decisions, and grow together. They're practical behaviors, not slogans, and they're part of how we hire, give feedback, and support one another every day.

We're looking for teammates who are excited to:

  • Stay curious and ask thoughtful questions.

  • Adapt when plans change.

  • Exercise good judgment rather than chase perfection.

  • Care for the success of the whole team, not just their own work.

  • Pursue ambitious goals while remaining humble enough to keep learning.

  • Commit fully to the shared adventure we're building together.

You'll Thrive Here If...

  • You enjoy asking questions before jumping to conclusions.

  • You adapt comfortably when priorities evolve.

  • You balance ambition with pragmatism.

  • You communicate thoughtfully and seek feedback.

  • You care about helping your teammates succeed.

  • You embrace uncertainty as part of creating something new.

Please Note: Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States or Canada. Gardens cannot assist with work authorizations or work visas. Applicants must also be willing to work within North American time zones (EST–PST).

  • Step 3: Panel Interview (3 - 1 Hour Sections)

  • Step 4: Gardeners Debrief

  • Step 5: Offer

Gardens is a fully distributed game studio founded by creators behind titles including Journey, What Remains of Edith Finch, Blaseball, Dustforce, Ashen, Guild Wars 2, Baldur’s Gate 3, and more.

We're developing our flagship project: a multiplayer fantasy adventure inspired by the friendships, discoveries, and unforgettable stories that emerge when people explore together.

We believe the best ideas come from teams with diverse experiences, perspectives, backgrounds, and ways of thinking. Every Gardener helps shape not only what we build, but how we build it.

Each of us arrives by a different path, bringing unique experiences, perspectives, and ways of seeing the world. That range is part of what makes our games and our studio better than any one of us could build alone.

Gardens is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities.

Research consistently shows that talented people, particularly women, people of color, and those from historically underrepresented communities are less likely to apply unless they meet every listed requirement. raw.title: Investor Network Manager
raw.excerpt: We are hiring an Investor Network Manager to grow the investor side of Paires, the network of family offices and high-net-worth individuals our founders raise from.
raw.description:
We are hiring an Investor Network Manager to grow the investor side of Paires, the network of family offices and high-net-worth individuals our founders raise from.

Paires is where founders come to raise capital. We pair them with the right investors from a large, engaged global investor network, then our agents manage the relationships that turn into meetings. It is a two-sided platform, live with paying clients, profitable and self-funded, built by a small, senior, flat team that ships fast.

The role

The network in your title is the heart of the platform, and your job is to grow it. The craft is allocator trust. You find the right family offices and HNWIs, earn the first conversation, and become the person whose calls get answered within a day. Month after month you open new relationships, match investors to live mandates, brief them properly before every meeting, and keep your book warm through honest work that never pushes.

If you have this craft, you have a book to show for it, and that book will let you contribute in your first weeks here. What Paires adds is everything a lone operator cannot offer their investors: a steady flow of curated opportunities, each one briefed and followed through. Your relationships become more valuable inside the platform, and the ones you build here compound on top. One thing this seat is not: technical. Our engineers build the platform and the agents. You work inside them, so your hours go to investors instead of admin.

What you will own

  • Your book. The allocator relationships you bring, plus the ones you build here, qualified, mapped, and kept active.

  • Growth on two tracks. Warm additions through your circle and referrals, and new allocators you open from scratch, from first touch to first allocation.

  • Mandate matching. The right investors paired with live deals, briefed before every meeting, their feedback captured after.

  • The standard. Your investors answer you within a day because you have earned it.

You are a fit if you

  • Know how to earn an allocator's trust and have done it before, in wealth management, private banking, a family office, placement, or your own advisory practice, and hold an active network of family offices and HNWIs to show for it.

  • Built that book yourself and can do it again. You have a working method for opening allocator relationships from nothing, and your network's origin story proves it.

  • Can contribute early. Your relationships are current and warm enough that mandate-fit allocators will take a call on your word.

  • Know direct deals. Your investors allocate to US startups at the growth stage, wherever in the world those investors sit, and you speak their screening language of thesis, check size, structure, and downside.

  • Qualify honestly. You can tell an allocator who deploys from one who takes polite meetings, and you protect everyone's time accordingly.

  • Treat discretion as a reflex. Names, allocations, and conversations stay confidential, always.

  • Work like it's 2026. You run your pipeline, briefs, and follow-ups inside modern AI tooling, so your hours go to relationships instead of admin.

What we offer

Fully remote and async. Your day overlaps with US Eastern time for a few hours, not full US hours. Meetings batch on Mondays and Thursdays, the rest is deep work. The best AI tooling, paid. A live deal flow your investors will thank you for, and a platform that multiplies what one person with good relationships can do alone.

How to apply: hit apply, which takes you to our short application form. We read every application. Do not include investor names anywhere in it. We evaluate composition, not contacts.

Job Title: MSP Technical Support Specialist

Location: Remote

Time Zone: 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM EST

Role Overview

We are looking for an enthusiastic and eager-to-learn Entry-Level IT Support Specialist to join our fast-paced Managed Services Provider (MSP) environment. In this role, you will serve as the first point of contact for inbound technical support requests, working alongside experienced engineers to deliver timely, accurate resolutions. If you are passionate about technology, eager to build your IT career, and ready to learn in a ticket-driven, SLA-focused setting, we want to hear from you.

What You'll Do

Receive, triage, and respond to inbound support tickets via phone, email, and ticketing platform within defined SLA windows.

raw.description:
Wyoming Rural Healthcare Finance and Revenue Cycle Leadership Opportunities

Rural Staffing Services partners with rural hospitals, clinics, public hospital districts, and community healthcare organizations throughout Wyoming to identify experienced finance and revenue cycle leaders who understand the unique realities of rural healthcare.

We are currently connecting with professionals who may be interested in active and upcoming finance, accounting, reimbursement, revenue cycle, billing, coding, and patient financial services leadership opportunities across Wyoming.

These opportunities may include leadership within Critical Access Hospitals, rural and community hospitals, Rural Health Clinics, Federally Qualified Health Centers, public hospital districts, long-term care organizations, and integrated rural healthcare systems.

Explore Rural Healthcare Opportunities at RSSJobs.org

This application may connect you with the specific opportunity you were viewing, as well as other current or upcoming rural healthcare positions throughout Wyoming that align with your experience and goals.

Visit to explore additional rural healthcare opportunities and communities.

This Is More Than a Finance Role

Strong financial and revenue cycle operations help protect healthcare access for an entire rural community.

These leaders ensure organizations can accurately capture revenue, manage resources responsibly, support employees, maintain compliance, and remain financially strong enough to continue caring for the people who depend on them.

In a rural healthcare organization, finance and revenue cycle leaders often work across departments and may have broader responsibilities than they would in a larger system. The strongest leaders understand how registration, coding, billing, reimbursement, patient accounts, accounting, and operational decisions connect to one another.

They are collaborative, detail-oriented, approachable, and able to turn complex financial information into practical guidance for employees, department leaders, executives, and governing boards.

Opportunities May Include

This application may connect you with current or upcoming roles such as:

  • Controller
  • Assistant Controller
  • Finance Director or Manager
  • Accounting Director or Manager
  • Revenue Cycle Director or Manager
  • Patient Financial Services Director or Manager
  • Patient Accounts Manager
  • Business Office Director or Manager
  • Billing Director or Manager
  • Coding Director, Manager, or Supervisor
  • Health Information Management revenue cycle leadership
  • Reimbursement Director or Manager
  • Chargemaster or Charge Description Master leadership
  • Accounts Payable or Accounts Receivable leadership
  • Payroll leadership
  • Senior billing, coding, or patient accounts supervisory roles

What You May Lead

Responsibilities will vary by organization and position and may include:

  • Leading accounting, finance, revenue cycle, billing, coding, or patient financial services functions
  • Supporting accurate and timely financial reporting
  • Managing month-end and year-end close processes
  • Developing budgets, forecasts, and financial performance reports
  • Strengthening billing, collections, cash flow, and reimbursement performance
  • Monitoring key revenue cycle metrics and identifying opportunities for improvement
  • Supporting accurate coding, charge capture, claims submission, and payment posting
  • Overseeing patient accounts, financial counseling, and collection processes
  • Ensuring compliance with payer, regulatory, accounting, and documentation requirements
  • Preparing for financial, coding, billing, or compliance audits
  • Developing policies, procedures, workflows, and internal controls
  • Training and supporting finance and revenue cycle employees
  • Collaborating with clinical, operational, IT, HIM, and executive leaders
  • Helping employees understand how their work affects organizational sustainability
  • Supporting system implementations, process improvements, or departmental restructuring

What You Will Bring

Qualifications will vary by opportunity, but organizations may seek:

  • Progressive experience in healthcare finance, accounting, revenue cycle, billing, coding, reimbursement, or patient financial services
  • Previous leadership experience as a director, manager, controller, supervisor, or comparable leader
  • Knowledge of healthcare reimbursement, payer requirements, billing practices, and financial operations
  • Experience with Medicare, Medicaid, commercial insurance, and patient-pay accounts
  • An understanding of hospital, clinic, or healthcare-system workflows
  • Experience analyzing financial or revenue cycle performance and communicating findings to leadership
  • Strong organizational, problem-solving, and team-development skills
  • Experience with Critical Access Hospitals, Rural Health Clinics, FQHCs, public hospital districts, or community healthcare organizations
  • Relevant education or professional credentials based on the position
  • A collaborative and relationship-focused leadership style

Some opportunities may prefer credentials such as CPA, CHFP, CRCR, CPC, CCS, RHIA, RHIT, or other finance, coding, revenue cycle, or health information certifications. Requirements will depend on the specific role.

Why Rural Wyoming?

Wyoming's rural healthcare organizations serve communities surrounded by mountains, high plains, ranchlands, rivers, open roads, and wide-open spaces. These organizations frequently operate with lean teams, limited resources, and a tremendous responsibility to the communities they serve.

Finance and revenue cycle leadership in a rural organization provides the opportunity to see the direct impact of your work. Improving a process, supporting a team, or strengthening reimbursement can help preserve services, protect jobs, and keep care available close to home.

Join the RSS Rural Talent Network

By applying through this page, you are joining the confidential Rural Staffing Services talent network. You may be considered for current or upcoming finance and revenue cycle leadership opportunities that align with your background, goals, location preferences, and availability.

Please include your resume and let us know:

  • Which Wyoming communities or regions you would consider
  • Whether you are open to relocation
  • Whether you are interested in permanent, interim, remote, fractional, or multiple types of opportunities
  • Which areas best match your experience, such as accounting, finance, billing, coding, reimbursement, patient accounts, or full revenue cycle
  • Your experience with rural hospitals, Critical Access Hospitals, public hospital districts, FQHCs, or community healthcare organizations
  • Which position or community you were viewing on RSSJobs.org

Our team personally reviews each application. When we identify an opportunity that may be a strong match, we will contact you directly to share more about the organization, community, responsibilities, and next steps.

Your information will be handled professionally and confidentially.

Discover More Rural Healthcare Opportunities

Visit to explore additional rural healthcare positions, leadership opportunities, and communities throughout Wyoming.

Work Where It Matters.

Built for Rural.

raw.description:
PermitFlow is redefining how America builds. We’re an applied AI company serving the nation’s builders, tackling one of the largest information challenges in the economy: understanding what can be built, where, and how. Our AI agent workforce helps the fastest-growing construction companies navigate everything from permitting and licensing to inspections and project closeouts – accelerating housing, clean-energy, and infrastructure development across the country.

Despite being a $1.6T industry, construction still suffers from massive delays, wasted capital, and lost opportunity. PermitFlow has already delivered unprecedented speed, accuracy, and visibility to over $20B in development, helping contractors reduce compliance time, de-risk projects, and scale with confidence.

As the U.S. enters a new capex supercycle across data centers, factories, housing, and renewables, joining PermitFlow means building the AI infrastructure at the core of every construction project driving the next wave of reindustrialization.

We’ve raised over $90M, most recently completing our Series B, from top-tier investors including Accel, Kleiner Perkins, Initialized, Y Combinator, Felicis, and Altos Ventures, with backing from leaders at OpenAI, Google, Procore, ServiceTitan, Zillow, PlanGrid, and Uber.

We're growing fast and the recruiting function needs to scale with us. As Recruiting Operations Manager, you'll partner directly with the Head of People to centralize process, establish standards, and build the infrastructure that keeps our recruiting engine running smoothly as we grow. You'll own the operating layer end to end and make sure recruiters, coordinators, and hiring managers are all working from the same playbook.

This is a role for someone who operates independently, moves quickly, and earns trust fast. You'll proactively identify opportunities and risks, make recommendations, align stakeholders, and execute at a high level without sacrificing accuracy. Strong attention to detail, clear communication, and a real command of change management are core to this role. You'll be a trusted partner to the Head of People and the connective tissue that makes the recruiting function feel seamless to everyone it touches.

This role reports to the Head of People and is based in our NYC office on a hybrid M/W/F schedule.

What You'll Do

  • Own Our Recruiting Systems: Serve as the primary owner and administrator of Ashby; configuring pipelines, building reports, driving adoption of underused features, and integrating with our broader stack (Claude, Fathom, and beyond). You don't just use AI tools; you build with them and ship automations that measurably change how the team operates.

  • Run the Data: Build and maintain the single source of truth for hiring across the company. Own funnel reporting and recruiter capacity models, and partner closely with our People Operations Manager on headcount planning and prioritization. You're skeptical of numbers until you've checked the filters, and you use data to problem-solve and influence decisions at every level of the org.

  • Define How We Operate: Codify ownership across the recruiting function on who closes, who schedules, who owns references and offers, and run weekly priorities + capacity cadence that keeps the team aligned without adding meeting bloat. Document everything, maintain SLAs, and build the rituals that support a smooth and fast paced recruiting engine.

  • Level Up Interview Infrastructure: Extend our gold-standard interview model across the org, launch interviewer training programs, build and maintain interview kits, and keep documentation clean and consistent. Champion structured, bias-mitigated hiring practices through ongoing calibration and education.

  • Navigate Compliance and Immigration: Own the recruiting side of immigration; managing candidate work authorization status, coordinating visa sponsorship timelines with our People Ops team and outside counsel, and ensuring hiring workflows stay compliant. You don't need to be an immigration expert, but you need to know enough to move candidates through without delays or missteps.

  • Drive Offer and Referral Consistency: Own the tooling, templates, and approval workflows that bring consistency and speed to our offer process. Partner with People Ops to enforce our comp framework across every offer and make sure nothing falls through the cracks. Own the referral program end to end, from process and tracking to messaging that actually gets used.

  • Champion Candidate Experience: Own candidate-comms SLAs end-to-end. Partner with the Head of People and Marketing to sharpen our EVP and maintain quality and consistency across every recruiting platform and touchpoint.

What We're Looking For

  • Bachelor's degree and 4+ years in recruiting operations or talent operations: Includes meaningful time in a high-growth or startup environment where you've built programs from scratch

  • Deep ATS expertise: Ashby strongly preferred; you've configured pipelines, built reports, owned automations, and led at least one major rollout

  • AI-native operator: You build with AI tools, not just use them; you've shipped prompts, automations, and AI-assisted workflows that have measurably changed how a team operates

  • Strong data instincts: Comfortable building funnel reports and capacity models from scratch; you use data to problem-solve and influence, not just report

  • Immigration program experience: Hands-on ownership of work authorization tracking, and visa sponsorship workflows

  • Familiarity with employment law compliance: You know where the guardrails are and build processes that stay inside them

  • Bias for action and urgency: You move fast, make decisions with imperfect information, and drive initiatives forward without waiting for direction

  • Exceptional communication and influencing skills: Trusted by executives, respected by recruiters and hiring managers, easy to partner with cross-functionally

  • Based in NYC: able to work in-office M/W/F alongside the leadership team

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity in a high-growth company.

  • 100% company-paid base medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees + healthcare FSA.

  • 401(k) savings plan.

  • Unlimited PTO and paid family leave.

  • Home office & equipment stipend.

  • Daily in-office lunch and dinner.

  • Commuter benefits (pre-tax transit and parking).

PermitFlow provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, or family status, as protected by applicable law.

We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities. All employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and business needs.

Compensation Range: $130K - $160K

Adventist Health Roseville and shared service teams have access to enjoy a welcoming space designed to promote well-being and inspire your best work.

Job Summary:

Performs quality reviews and audits to ensure compliance with DRG validation, ICD-10/PCS, and CPT coding guidelines. Coordinates with department leadership to ensure standards are met in accordance with department and organization policy. Contributes to improving the processes and infrastructure of the department. Demonstrates proficiency in facilitation and interpersonal communication, organizational skills, prioritization of tasks, professionalism, and educating and training as required. Uses in depth understanding of the CQR quality workplan to will promote compliance and awareness of the plan. Acts as a subject matter expert (SME) in national coding guidelines for hospital inpatient and/or outpatient and will ensure compliance with those guidelines along with all company coding policies. Uses performance improvement analyses to improve the accuracy, integrity and quality of patient data, ensure minimal variation in coding practices, and improve the quality of physician documentation within the body of the medical record to support code assignments which results in appropriate reimbursement and data integrity.

Job Requirements:

Education and Work Experience:

  • High School Education/GED or equivalent: Required
  • Associate’s/Technical Degree or equivalent combination of education/related experience: Preferred
  • Five years' acute care inpatient and/or outpatient coding experience: Required
  • Three years' coding auditing/monitoring experience: Preferred

Licenses/Certifications:

  • Certified Coding Specialist credential through AHIMA: Required
  • Certified Coding Specialist (CCS): Required

Essential Functions:

  • Performs regularly scheduled quality reviews and audits per departmental policies and procedures (routine, pre-bill, policy driven, targeted, and post-bill) for hospital inpatient and/or outpatient coding. Facilitates the coder audit appeal process, providing rationale and education to the coding team as required. Performs ad hoc quality reviews, such as targeted DRG reviews, and special projects as assigned by management.
  • Prepares detailed audit reports outlining findings, recommendations, rationale, and corrective actions needed. Facilitates the coder appeal process. Assists team members with coding questions and provide resolution guidance.
  • Assists in ensuring coding staff adherence with coding guidelines and policy, both internal and vendor teams. Demonstrates and applies expert level knowledge of medical coding practices and concepts. Communicates appropriately with manager and all stakeholders as required.
  • Identifies and communicates educational opportunities to manager. Maintains working knowledge of workflows, systems, and tools used in the department. Reviews all official data quality standards, coding guidelines, company policies and procedures, and clinical/medical resources to assure coding knowledge and skills remain current.
  • Maintains up-to-date knowledge of medical terminology, coding guidelines, quality standards, regulatory changes, etc. that affect the audit process. Assists in creation and maintenance of a positive working environment, including effective communication and setting an appropriate professional example.
  • Performs other job-related duties as assigned.

Organizational Requirements:

Adventist Health is committed to the safety and wellbeing of our associates and patients. Therefore, we require that all associates receive all required vaccinations as a condition of employment and annually thereafter, where applicable. Medical and religious exemptions may apply.

Adventist Health participates in E-Verify. Visit for more information about E-Verify. By choosing to apply, you acknowledge that you have accessed and read the E-Verify Participation and Right to Work notices and understand the contents therein.

About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

About the Job

We are looking for a 3D Animator to lead the creation of high-quality 3D animations, visual storytelling, and motion content across BJAK’s marketing, product, and brand initiatives.

In this role, you will bring concepts to life through compelling animation, character performance, camera work, environmental storytelling, and cinematic visuals. You will work closely with creative, marketing, and product teams to create engaging content that elevates the BJAK brand while mentoring junior artists and helping define animation standards across the organization.

Key Responsibilities

3D Animation & Creative Execution

  • Create high-quality 3D animations for marketing campaigns, product showcases, social media content, and brand storytelling.

  • Develop engaging character, object, and environmental animations that communicate ideas effectively.

  • Translate storyboards and creative concepts into polished 3D animated content.

  • Produce cinematic camera movements, transitions, and visual sequences that enhance audience engagement.

  • Ensure consistency in animation quality, visual style, and brand identity across all deliverables.

Creative Direction & Collaboration

  • Collaborate closely with Creative, Marketing, Product, and Content teams to develop compelling visual narratives.

  • Contribute to concept development, storyboarding, and creative ideation sessions.

  • Mentor and provide guidance to junior animators and designers.

  • Work alongside motion designers, video editors, illustrators, and creative producers to deliver cohesive multimedia campaigns.

  • Present animation concepts and creative solutions to stakeholders.

Technical Excellence

  • Manage the end-to-end 3D production pipeline, including modeling, rigging, animation, lighting, rendering, compositing, and post-production.

  • Optimize workflows, rendering processes, and asset management systems.

  • Develop reusable animation assets, templates, and production standards.

  • Troubleshoot technical issues related to animation, rendering, simulation, or visual effects.

  • Ensure projects are delivered on time while maintaining exceptional creative quality.

Innovation & Emerging Technologies

  • Stay current with industry trends in 3D animation, CGI, motion graphics, and visual effects.

  • Explore new tools, workflows, AI-assisted creative technologies, and real-time rendering techniques.

  • Experiment with advanced animation techniques, simulations, and cinematic storytelling approaches.

  • Continuously elevate BJAK’s visual content standards through innovation and creative excellence.

Requirements

  • Diploma or Bachelor's degree in Animation, Multimedia Design, Computer Graphics, Visual Effects, or a related field.

  • 2+ years of professional experience in 3D animation, CGI production, motion graphics, or visual storytelling.

  • Expert proficiency in Blender, Cinema 4D, Maya, or equivalent 3D software.

  • Strong experience with lighting, rendering, compositing, and animation pipelines.

  • Proficiency in Adobe After Effects, Premiere Pro, Photoshop, and related creative tools.

  • Strong understanding of animation principles, timing, weight, movement, and storytelling.

  • Experience creating high-quality character, product, or environment animations.

  • Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

  • Excellent communication, collaboration, and creative problem-solving skills.

  • A strong portfolio or showreel demonstrating advanced 3D animation work is required.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Unreal Engine, Houdini, or real-time rendering workflows.

  • Knowledge of character rigging, simulations, dynamics, and visual effects.

  • Experience integrating AI-assisted creative tools into animation workflows.

  • Background in advertising, digital products, technology, fintech, or startup environments.

Location

  • This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Sweden. We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Sweden.


Language

  • English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

  • Due to the nature of the work, US citizenship is required

  • 5+ years’ experience managing CWM task order work for USACE Huntsville Center strongly preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to manage projects to scope, schedule, and budget
  • Knowledge of project financial accounting, reporting, and controls
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including both oral and written
  • Organizational management skills and ability to perform detail-oriented work
  • Experienced on MMR programs, including CWM and advanced geophysical classification
  • Experience managing CWM projects for the USACE Huntsville Center and/or Redstone Arsenal.
  • Demonstrated proposal-writing skills, Multiple Award Task Order Contract proposals
  • Demonstrated ability to market and win work successfully and effectively
  • Advanced knowledge of DoD and USACE MMR focusing on CWM requirements and processes
  • Excellent and relevant references
  • Position may require travel

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

Despite this, there's been very little innovation over the past 70 years in how materials, which constitute up to 40% of project costs, are bought and sold. This is our opportunity.

About the Role

LATAM engineering hiring isn't the quiet, cost-driven move it used to be. More and more AI and software companies are standing up permanent engineering centers across the region, and senior placements have overtaken junior ones. We're doubling down on LATAM technical talent with a Mexico City office in 2027.

This is a chance to own technical recruiting for that build, and sharpen our technical recruiting motion as that bet gets bigger. This hire will be the sole technical recruiter at Kojo with real authority over how we compete for engineering talent in one of the fastest-moving, least-understood talent markets in tech right now.

You partner directly with engineering leadership, work alongside a recruiting coordinator so the logistics don't fall on you alone, and partner with our Director of Talent to hold an increasingly heightened talent bar that determines who builds Kojo's product.

What you'll own

  • Run full-cycle, white-glove recruiting for Kojo's LATAM engineering org, plus occasional NA-based technical searches when they come up.

  • Build an evergreen, competitive outbound pipeline of A+ engineers, identifying high-talent-density teams and coaching hiring managers on how to go after passive candidates the rest of the market isn't reaching.

  • Hold the bar high enough that engineering leadership trusts every name you bring them, and say so when a panel is about to settle.

  • Keep Ashby clean enough that anyone on the team can trust it without a second look.

  • Work AI-natively: Claude, Granola, Ashby, LinkedIn Recruiter's AI features, and emerging sourcing tools are part of how you source, screen, and manage pipeline day to day, not an occasional shortcut.

Representative Projects

  • Built the outbound engine behind Kojo's first wave of LATAM engineering hires, senior-heavy from day one, with next to no inbound volume to lean on.

  • Closed a senior engineer against a competing offer from a company paying well above what the market usually requires.

  • Earned enough trust with an engineering leadership team that they started asking for you by name.

About You

You've watched LATAM engineering hiring go from a quiet advantage to one of the most contested plays in tech, and you want to be the person who masters it while everyone else is still catching up. This is the kind of role that turns into a specialty, and a reputation. If you'd rather build the pipeline nobody else has than work off whoever applies, we should talk.

What we're looking for

  • Exceptional ownership and agency to proactively identify pipeline gaps, create momentum on stalled searches, make sound calls with imperfect information, and consistently drive every search across the finish line without waiting for direction (3+ years of full-cycle or coordination recruiting experience required).

  • A keen eye for who's truly great, on and off the resume, and a real stake in whether a hire turns out to be a top performer, not just whether a role gets filled.

  • Proven outbound sourcing credibility, whether it’s a fluency in LinkedIn Recruiter or another sourcing funnel. The most impactful business partners have real opinions on target companies, who's overpaying, who just had layoffs, and where the best underrated senior engineers are, especially now that everyone else is chasing the same names.

  • Technical fluency in the roles you’re hiring for, knowing enough about engineering to earn a Director of Engineering's trust, fast.

  • Genuine care, showing up for candidates as a trusted resource in the market, not simply an interview scheduler

  • Proven stakeholder partnership where hiring managers treat you as part of their team, not an outside vendor filling a req.

  • Someone who wants to be shadowed, takes feedback as fuel, and cares about the recruiting team's success as much as your own.

  • English fluency, since you'll work daily with NA-based engineering leadership and hiring managers.

What you care about

  • Customer Obsession: A candidate's experience is a business need, not a box to check after hours.

  • Passion: You take real pride in who you hire, not just that a role got filled.

  • Accountability: You call out when a panel's about to settle, and you own a search's outcome like it's yours.

Working at Kojo

Salary: Your salary will be dependent upon many factors, including your experience level, skillset, market dynamics and balancing internal equity relative to other Kojo employees. The compensation and benefits information that we provide is based on Kojo’s good-faith estimate as of the date of the job posting and may be modified in the future.

Benefits: This position is also eligible for a new hire equity grant and all US-based full time employees are eligible for our full suite of perks and benefits. For more information about our perks and benefits, check out

Location: Kojo’s team members work from home 100% of the time across North and South America. If applicable, we’ll identify the travel and/or location-specific requirements of a position in the text above. Otherwise, team members can expect to work business hours congruent with their local time zone and remotely.

Inclusive Workplace: Kojo values diverse perspectives and is committed to building an inclusive workplace. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and do not discriminate on the basis of sex, race, color, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, citizenship, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We strongly encourage people from underrepresented groups to apply.



Scam Notice: Please be aware that there are individuals and organizations that may attempt to scam job seekers by offering fraudulent employment opportunities in the name of Kojo. These scams may involve fake job postings, unsolicited emails, or messages claiming to be from our recruiters or hiring managers. Kojo will never ask for any personal account information, such credit card details or bank account numbers, during the recruitment process.

Role Title: Medical Writer / Clinical Document Author

Role Type: Contractor

Location: Remote

micro1 is engaging Medical Writers / Clinical Document Authors to participate in a customer’s project focused on developing advanced AI-assisted writing tools for clinical documentation. In this role, you'll apply your expertise to help train next-generation AI systems. Your work will shape how models learn, reason, and perform through high-quality, real-world input. No prior experience in AI is required — your domain knowledge is what matters.

Scope of Work

  1. Author and review realistic evaluation tasks based on Clinical Study Reports, DSURs, PSURs/PBRERs, and related clinical documents to inform AI tool development.
  2. Apply expert judgment to assess whether AI-generated content fulfills clinical template and structural requirements, including ICH E3 organization, section sequencing, cross-referencing, and appendix management.
  3. Evaluate scientific accuracy in narrative sections such as efficacy, safety summaries, discussion, and conclusions, distinguishing true scientific or interpretive errors from stylistic differences.
  4. Trace narrative claims to source records—tables, figures, listings, and protocols—to verify that all assertions are appropriately supported.
  5. Provide clear and structured written rationales for each assessment, enabling precise diagnosis and improvement of AI model behavior.
  6. Collaborate with project leads to refine evaluation frameworks and document best practices for clinical regulatory writing in the context of AI.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Minimum 5 years of regulatory medical writing experience at a sponsor, CRO, or as an independent consultant.
  2. Direct experience independently authoring or leading the authoring of full Clinical Study Reports, beyond summaries or partial contributions.
  3. Fluency with ICH E3 and conventions for periodic safety documentation (ICH E2F, ICH E2C) and eCTD placement.
  4. Demonstrated ability to read and interpret TFLs and protocol documents, identifying where narrative diverges from source data.
  5. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, especially in providing structured, actionable feedback on clinical content.
  6. Advanced degree in life sciences, pharmacy, or medicine (PhD, PharmD, MD, MSc), or equivalent depth of authoring experience.
  7. Experience across multiple clinical phases and therapeutic areas; oncology and haematology expertise is especially valued.

Join our customer's team and leverage your authoring expertise to help design the next generation of AI-assisted clinical documentation solutions. This high-bar role offers you the chance to shape how tomorrow's writing teams draft and review regulatory documents — through your expert input, judgment, and real-world experience.

raw.description:
Staff Accountant

Snapshot of Curvion Blue

Curvion Blue is a high-performance revenue operations and sales augmentation company that helps businesses build, optimize, and scale their revenue engines.

We operate in a fast-moving environment with numerous companies, brands, offers, sales teams, vendors, and revenue relationships moving through our financial systems. Our accounting function needs to be accurate, organized, proactive, and capable of handling complexity at scale.

We're looking for a Staff Accountant who is more than a transaction processor. We need someone who can own day-to-day accounting responsibilities, manage a high volume of financial activity, reconcile complex transactions, accurately administer commissions, and identify issues before they become problems.

Experience in an agency, BPO, outsourced accounting firm, SaaS company, sales organization, marketplace, or another high-volume financial environment is highly preferred.

Position Overview

The Staff Accountant is responsible for maintaining accurate, timely, and well-documented financial records across Curvion Blue's operations.

This role supports a high-volume, multi-company financial environment where billing, revenue, payments, and sales commissions flow across dozens of external companies, brands, offers, and revenue relationships.

The Staff Accountant will own or support core accounting workflows across:

  • Accounts payable

  • Accounts receivable

  • Billing and invoicing

  • Revenue reconciliation

  • Sales commissions

  • Payroll and commission schedules

  • Credit cards and expenses

  • Cash and banking

  • Account reconciliations

  • Month-end close

  • Financial reporting support

The right person is highly organized, analytical, detail-oriented, and comfortable working independently. They should be able to look across large amounts of financial data and quickly identify when something doesn't tie out, doesn't make sense, or doesn't match the underlying agreement.

You should naturally ask:

"What should this number be, and why isn't it?"

rather than simply entering what is in front of you.

You SHOULD Apply If

  • You have experience managing high-volume accounting activity across multiple companies, entities, customers, vendors, or revenue streams.

  • You have experience with sales commissions, variable compensation, or commission reconciliation.

  • You have experience with billing, invoicing, AR, and revenue reconciliation.

  • You are comfortable working with large amounts of transactional data.

  • You have worked in an agency, BPO, outsourced accounting firm, SaaS company, sales organization, marketplace, or other fast-paced environment.

  • You are exceptionally detail-oriented and naturally notice when something doesn't reconcile.

  • You can investigate discrepancies rather than simply flagging them.

  • You can manage recurring deadlines without constant follow-up.

  • You are comfortable working independently in a remote environment.

  • You communicate quickly when something is wrong or when you need additional information.

  • You enjoy improving processes rather than simply following them.

  • You can move quickly without sacrificing accuracy.

You SHOULD NOT Apply If

  • You need someone to give you a checklist for every task.

  • You have only worked in low-volume accounting environments and are uncomfortable with a high volume of transactions.

  • You have little experience with reconciliations or investigating discrepancies.

  • You consider accounting "done" once transactions have been entered.

  • You regularly discover problems only after someone else points them out.

  • You struggle to manage competing deadlines.

  • You are uncomfortable working with commission calculations or variable compensation.

  • You prefer highly repetitive work with little ownership or problem-solving.

  • You are not comfortable communicating proactively in a remote environment.

What You'll Own

Accounts Payable

  • Maintain accurate AP records and trackers as invoices are received.

  • Review invoices for accuracy, coding, approvals, and appropriate documentation.

  • Process electronic payments and checks according to established approval procedures.

  • Maintain accurate vendor records and contact information.

  • Collect and maintain current W-9s and applicable vendor documentation.

  • Validate vendor banking information before electronic payments are initiated.

  • Monitor outstanding payables and ensure payments are processed on schedule.

  • Identify unusual, duplicate, or potentially fraudulent transactions and escalate appropriately.

Accounts Receivable & Billing

  • Create and distribute invoices according to established billing schedules and agreements.

  • Reconcile customer payments against invoices and supporting documentation.

  • Maintain accurate customer and company records.

  • Monitor outstanding receivables and support collection efforts.

  • Investigate payment discrepancies, unapplied cash, short payments, and billing variances.

  • Reconcile amounts billed and collected against applicable contracts, SOWs, agreements, or other supporting documentation.

  • Identify billing issues before they become larger collection or revenue problems.

  • Support accurate revenue reporting across multiple companies and revenue streams.

Sales Commissions

  • Prepare and maintain commission schedules across multiple companies, brands, offers, and compensation structures.

  • Calculate commissions accurately based on applicable agreements, sales activity, payment status, and other compensation requirements.

  • Reconcile commission calculations against source data and supporting documentation.

  • Investigate discrepancies between sales activity, revenue collected, and commissions owed.

  • Maintain accurate records of commission calculations and supporting documentation.

  • Prepare commission schedules for review and approval.

  • Coordinate with internal stakeholders when commission information is incomplete or inconsistent.

  • Identify recurring commission issues and recommend process improvements.

Payroll & Compensation

  • Prepare payroll and commission schedules for review and approval.

  • Process approved payroll accurately and according to established deadlines.

  • Reconcile payroll activity against accounting records.

  • Review variable compensation calculations and supporting documentation for accuracy.

  • Investigate discrepancies and escalate unresolved issues promptly.

  • Maintain appropriate documentation for payroll and compensation transactions.

Credit Cards & Expenses

  • Enter and categorize credit card transactions accurately.

  • Collect and maintain receipts and supporting documentation.

  • Reconcile credit card activity to monthly statements.

  • Identify missing receipts, unusual transactions, duplicate charges, or coding discrepancies.

  • Ensure credit card payments are processed by their due dates.

  • Reconcile employee reimbursements against supporting documentation.

Cash & Banking

  • Reconcile bank transactions to accounting records and supporting documentation.

  • Investigate discrepancies and ensure issues are resolved promptly.

  • Monitor cash activity and identify unusual or unexpected transactions.

  • Maintain accurate cash flow reporting and forecasts.

  • Reconcile intercompany activity where applicable.

  • Ensure bank and cash balances are properly reflected in the financial records.

Month-End Close

  • Own assigned components of the month-end close process and meet established deadlines.

  • Perform initial P&L reviews and identify unusual fluctuations or inconsistencies.

  • Prepare journal entries and supporting documentation.

  • Reconcile balance sheet accounts to source documents and subledgers.

  • Review financial activity for completeness and accuracy.

  • Prepare draft financial reporting packages and supporting schedules.

  • Review financial results against contracts, invoices, payroll, commissions, and other source documentation.

  • Roll forward recurring schedules and maintain accurate month-end workbooks.

  • Support quarterly and annual accounting requirements, including sales tax and year-end reporting.

  • Document changes to processes and accounting procedures.

Financial Accuracy & Controls

You will be expected to serve as an additional layer of quality control within the accounting function.

That means you will:

  • Review transactional data for irregularities, unusual activity, and inconsistencies.

  • Investigate discrepancies rather than simply correcting the symptom.

  • Maintain clean and complete supporting documentation.

  • Protect confidential financial, payroll, employee, and company information.

  • Safeguard accounting system access and credentials.

  • Monitor for potential fraud and escalate concerns immediately.

  • Maintain clear audit trails and documentation.

  • Identify opportunities to improve financial controls and reduce errors.

  • Research accounting questions and applicable rules when necessary.

  • Recommend improvements to accounting processes, systems, and controls.

You SHOULD Be Comfortable With

  • High-volume transaction environments.

  • Managing financial activity across dozens of companies, customers, vendors, or revenue relationships.

  • Sales commissions and variable compensation.

  • Billing and revenue reconciliation.

  • Multiple recurring deadlines.

  • AP and AR workflows.

  • Payroll and commission cycles.

  • Bank and balance sheet reconciliations.

  • Month-end close.

  • Identifying and investigating discrepancies.

  • Working with contracts, SOWs, invoices, and other financial source documentation.

  • Remote collaboration and asynchronous communication.

  • Learning new financial systems and technology quickly.

  • Building and improving accounting processes.

What Success Looks Like

First 30 Days

  • Understand Curvion Blue's accounting structure, systems, companies, offers, and financial workflows.

  • Build strong working relationships with the Accounting Manager, Controller, and key internal stakeholders.

  • Learn the company's billing, commission, reconciliation, and close processes.

  • Consistently meet assigned deadlines.

  • Demonstrate strong attention to detail and follow-through.

First 60 Days

  • Independently own recurring accounting responsibilities.

  • Consistently maintain accurate AP, AR, billing, commission, banking, credit card, and reconciliation workflows.

  • Identify discrepancies proactively and communicate issues before they become problems.

  • Demonstrate strong command of the company's accounting systems and processes.

  • Reliably manage multiple companies, revenue streams, and competing priorities.

First 90 Days

  • Reliably own assigned accounting functions with minimal oversight.

  • Consistently deliver accurate work on time, including during month-end close.

  • Accurately manage commission and revenue reconciliation across a high volume of transactions.

  • Proactively identify opportunities to improve accounting processes and controls.

  • Demonstrate the ability to manage complexity without sacrificing accuracy.

  • Become someone the Accounting Manager and Controller can trust to see the problem before it becomes a fire drill.

Primary Performance KPIs

  • 100% on-time completion of assigned accounting deadlines.

  • 98%+ accuracy across assigned accounting workflows.

  • 100% completion of assigned month-end close responsibilities by deadline.

  • 100% of assigned reconciliations completed accurately and on schedule.

  • 98%+ accuracy across commission calculations and schedules.

  • Zero avoidable late payments resulting from missed accounting deadlines.

  • Timely identification and escalation of material discrepancies.

  • Complete and organized supporting documentation for assigned transactions and reconciliations.

  • Consistent adherence to accounting controls and established processes.

Communication & Ownership Expectations

  • Communicate accounting issues promptly rather than allowing them to linger.

  • Respond to internal communications within one business day, even when the final answer is still pending.

  • Clearly communicate competing priorities, blockers, and deadlines.

  • Keep the Accounting Manager and Controller informed of material discrepancies or unusual activity.

  • Take ownership of assigned responsibilities from beginning to end.

  • Proactively follow up on outstanding information required to complete accounting responsibilities.

  • Maintain confidentiality around financial, payroll, employee, and company information.

  • Work effectively in a remote environment with high levels of autonomy.

  • Maintain accurate records, calendars, task lists, and deadlines.

  • Escalate issues when appropriate while making a reasonable effort to investigate and resolve them independently first.

Qualifications

Required

  • 3+ years of accounting experience.

  • Strong understanding of general accounting principles.

  • Experience with AP, AR, billing, reconciliations, and month-end close.

  • Experience working with high-volume financial transactions.

  • Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills.

  • Exceptional attention to detail and organization.

  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple deadlines.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Highly Preferred

  • Experience with sales commissions or variable compensation.

  • Experience reconciling revenue, payments, commissions, or billing across multiple companies or revenue streams.

  • Experience in an agency, BPO, outsourced accounting, fractional accounting, SaaS, marketplace, or sales environment.

  • Experience working with US-based companies or US GAAP.

  • Experience managing financial activity across multiple entities or business relationships.

  • Experience with contract/SOW-based billing.

  • Experience with accounting software such as QuickBooks Online, Xero, NetSuite, or similar platforms.

  • Experience with systems such as Gusto, , Ramp, Brex, Stripe, or similar financial platforms.

  • Experience supporting a rapidly growing company.

The Bottom Line

We're not looking for someone whose definition of success is simply:

"I completed my accounting tasks."

We're looking for someone who takes ownership of the financial operation, keeps the numbers clean, catches inconsistencies, understands the relationship between revenue and commissions, meets deadlines, communicates proactively, and continuously looks for ways to make the accounting function better.

This role is a great fit for someone who enjoys complexity, volume, and problem-solving.

If you're the kind of accountant who sees a number that doesn't make sense and can't leave it alone until you figure out why, we want to talk to you.

This job requires working 9am-6pm PST hours and time zone

The Pharmacy Support Call Center Representative is primarily responsible for fielding requests such as: card activation, program eligibility, explanation of program benefit and explanation/troubleshooting of submission rejection.
